root_cause.text: In `drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_sync.c`, `xe_sync_entry_parse()` failed to release the acquired user fence reference when `dma_fence_chain_alloc()` returned `NULL`, causing a reference leak on the allocation-failure error path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (!sync->ufence_chain_fence) return -ENOMEM;` to `err = -ENOMEM; goto free_sync;`, showing the original early return bypassed cleanup of `sync->ufence`/user-fence resources, which the commit message explicitly says needed to be “properly release[d] ... to prevent a memory leak.”

intent_record.what: In xe_sync_entry_parse(), the direct return of -ENOMEM after dma_fence_chain_alloc() fails was replaced with setting err = -ENOMEM and jumping to the free_sync cleanup path instead of returning immediately.
intent_record.how: On allocation failure, the function now routes through the existing cleanup logic, allowing previously allocated resources in the sync parsing path to be released before the error is returned, preventing a resource leak or partial-state cleanup omission.

Author: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 31 16:40:45 2025 -0700

    drm/xe: Enforce correct user fence signaling order using
    
    Prevent application hangs caused by out-of-order fence signaling when
    user fences are attached. Use drm_syncobj (via dma-fence-chain) to
    guarantee that each user fence signals in order, regardless of the
    signaling order of the attached fences. Ensure user fence writebacks to
    us
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct from the root cause is not present in this version. In the shown parse path, the code now allocates a chain fence and immediately handles failure: `sync->ufence_chain_fence = dma_fence_chain_alloc(); if (!sync->ufence_chain_fence) return -ENOMEM;`. The reported leak was specifically that `xe_sync_entry_parse()` failed to release the acquired user fence reference when `dma_fence_chain_alloc()` returned `NULL`, but this snippet does not show any missing `user_fence_put()` on that error path, and the cleanup path has also been updated with `dma_fence_chain_free(sync->ufence_chain_fence);` and `if (!IS_ERR_OR_NULL(sync->ufence)) user_fence_put(sync->ufence);`. Since the bug condition is absent in the provided code and the relevant cleanup logic is present, this version is fixed.
